after.title: Preprint: Persistent or recurrent depression in young adults: associations with systemic inflammation and early life adversity.
after.authors: Shepherd, F. R.; Fairweather, S. J.; Howe, L. D.; Jones, H. J.; Khandaker, G. M.
after.abstract: Background There is limited research on persistent or recurrent depression into young adulthood. We examined the prevalence of recurrent/persistent depression in young adults, and associations with childhood trauma/adversity and systemic inflammation, and if inflammatory markers mediated associations between childhood trauma and subsequent depression. Methods ALSPAC participants with ICD-10 depression assessments at ages 18, 24 and 30 were classified as never depressed, transiently depressed (one episode), or persistently/recurrently depressed ([≥] 2). Trauma/adversity from birth to age 16/17 was characterised by type, timing and burden. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and C-reactive protein (CRP) were measured at ages 9, 16, 18 and 24. Analyses used multinomial logistic regression, linear regression and causal mediation models. Results Among 2,014 participants, 78.9% were never depressed, 15.0% had transient depression and 6.1% had persistent/recurrent depression. Trauma/adversity was more strongly associated with persistent/recurrent depression (RRR 3.17, 95% CI 1.98-5.06; FDR-P=6.2x10^-6) than transient depression, with a dose-response pattern and stronger associations for threat adversities. Middle-to-late childhood (11-17 yrs) emerged as a sensitive period for persistent/recurrent (RRR 2.85, 95% CI 1.47-5.52) and transient depression (RRR 1.85, 95% CI 1.25-2.73). Trauma/adversity was associated with modestly higher IL-6 at age 24 (all FDR-adjusted P < 0.05); CRP associations did not survive multiple-testing correction. Neither marker mediated trauma/adversity associations with persistent/recurrent depression. Conclusion Persistent/recurrent depression affects approximately 1 in 20 young adults. Childhood trauma/adversity, particularly during middle-to-late childhood, was associated with persistent/recurrent depression, but measured inflammatory proteins did not mediate this association. Further work is needed to understand biological mechanisms underlying the embedding early life psychosocial stress.

after.authors: Jarvensivu, E.; Jarvensivu, L.; Viitanen, M.; Rahkonen, O.; Lallukka, T.
after.abstract: Introduction: Socioeconomic differences in body mass index (BMI) are well established, but less is known about gender differences and their behavioral pathways. We examined gender differences in the association between socioeconomic position (SEP) and BMI, and whether dietary factors and physical activity mediated the associations. Methods: We used survey data from the employees of the City of Helsinki aged 19-39 collected in 2017 (n = 4,400, 80% women). SEP was measured by highest educational attainment, and the examined mediators were consumption of fruit and vegetables, red and processed meat, sweets and confectionery and alcohol as well as leisure-time vigorous physical activity (VPA) and sedentary time. We conducted gender-specific multiple mediation analyses using structural equation modeling and additional analyses using multiple imputation by chained equations. Results: With increasing educational attainment, mean BMI decreased from 26.4 kg/m2 to 24.0 kg/m2 among women, and from 26.6 kg/m2 to 25.2 kg/m2 among men. Lower SEP was associated with lower consumption of fruit and vegetables, higher consumption of red and processed meat, and lower VPA in both genders. Women reported healthier diets but less VPA than men. The strongest SEP-BMI mediator among women was VPA (indirect effect: 0.35, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.26, 0.44), followed by fruit and vegetable consumption (0.15, 95% CI 0.08, 0.23) and red and processed meat consumption (0.06, 95% CI 0.02, 0.11). Among men, significant mediators were red and processed meat consumption (0.12, 95% CI 0.03, 0.23), sedentary time (0.11, 95% CI 0.01, 0.24) and VPA (0.10, 95% CI 0.02, 0.21). Conclusions: Socioeconomic inequalities in BMI appear stronger among women and are shaped through partly different mechanisms between genders. Improving VPA may be relevant among low-SEP women, whereas reducing sedentary time may be more relevant among low-SEP men. Reducing red and processed meat is beneficial for both genders.

after.authors: Sisaye, A. M.; Hailemariam, M. D.
after.abstract: Background: The 2024-25 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) is Ethiopia's first national survey to measure early childhood development using UNICEF's Early Childhood Development Index 2030 (ECDI2030). This provides a national estimate for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 4.2.1, the proportion of children aged 24-59 months who are developmentally on track. We estimated the prevalence of being developmentally on track and examined its child, maternal, household and community determinants in Ethiopia. Methods: This cross-sectional study analysed 3,731 children aged 24-59 months (weighted n = 3,514) of 3,232 mothers in 771 clusters. Children were on track if they achieved the age-specific minimum number of the 20 ECDI2030 milestones. Prevalence was estimated with design-based methods. Four three-level mixed-effects logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) were fitted, and interviewer effects were assessed. Results: Overall, 36.3% (95% CI 33.4-39.3) of children were developmentally on track. Prevalence ranged from 23.3% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 77.7% in Addis Ababa. In the null model, 21.5% of the variation lay between clusters (median odds ratio 3.24). In the final model, the odds of being on track were lower at 36-47 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 0.57, 95% CI 0.44-0.74) and 48-59 months (AOR 0.39, 0.30-0.51) than at 24-35 months. They were also lower after a preceding birth interval under 24 months (AOR 0.75, 0.57-0.99), after recent diarrhoea, fever or cough (AOR 0.59, 0.45-0.77), and where distance to a health facility was a big problem (AOR 0.61, 0.48-0.79). Odds were higher for girls (AOR 1.38, 1.12-1.70), with maternal education (more than secondary vs none: AOR 2.08, 1.19-3.63) and with weekly media exposure (AOR 2.15, 1.51-3.06). The covariates explained 55.9% of the between-cluster variance. Conclusions: Nearly two in three Ethiopian children aged 24-59 months are not developmentally on track, and children fall further behind as they age. Interventions should target maternal education, access to information and health services, birth spacing and childhood illness, with priority for the lowest-performing regions and communities.

after.title: Preprint: Early Prediction of Discharge Outcomes in Geriatric Rehabilitation: Development and Temporal Validation of a Multiclass Model
after.authors: Kurzweil, E.; Hefetz, R.; Yanover, C.; Galor, I.; Markovitz, N.; Goldshtein, I.
after.author_corresponding_institution: KI research institute, Hod Hasharon, Israel
after.abstract: To develop and validate a model that predicts on day 7 of subacute rehabilitation (timed to inform the first multidisciplinary team meeting) the probabilities of three mutually exclusive outcomes: minimal dependency, nursing-care dependency, or medical deterioration. Design: Retrospective cohort study with temporal validation. Multinomial regression and XGBoost models were trained on 80% of admissions during the years 2016-2024 of members of the largest national health maintenance organization (HMO), tested on the remaining 20% and members of other HMOs, and validated on year 2025 admissions. Models output patient-level outcome probabilities with the strongest feature contributors. Setting: A public geriatric rehabilitation hospital. Participants: All consecutive first admissions (N=10,920; median age 80 years; median length of stay 35 days). Interventions: Not applicable. Main Outcome Measures: Discharge disposition: minimal dependency, nursing-care dependency, or medical deterioration (transfer to acute care without return, or in-hospital death). Predictors were demographic, functional, cognitive, clinical, and laboratory variables documented before day 7 with linkage to pre-admission community health records. Performance was assessed by multiclass area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score and positive predictive value (PPV). Results: Overall, 34% of patients were discharged with minimal dependency, 44% with nursing-care dependency, and 22% deteriorated medically. Both models performed comparably. Multinomial regression achieved an AUC of 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.83) compared with 0.72 (0.71-0.73) for FIM alone, and it was maintained on temporal validation (AUC 0.80, 0.78-0.82). At a [≥]60% probability threshold, the model flagged 32% of patients for nursing-care dependency and 5% for deterioration, with PPVs of 72% and 69%, respectively. Conclusions: Day-7 multiclass risk estimation from routinely collected data is feasible, interpretable and stable over time. Alerts could prompt earlier social-work involvement and closer monitoring of patients at risk of deterioration; prospective controlled evaluation is warranted.

after.authors: Setiabudiawan, T. P.; Iswandari, N.; Korompis, M.; Koesoemadinata, R. C.; Susandi, E.; Kulsum, I. D.; Turbawaty, D. K.; Alisjahbana, B.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Research Center for Care and Control of Infectious Diseases, Universitas Padjadjaran, Bandung, Indonesia
after.abstract: Background: TB eradication strategies in high burden countries need affordable, scalable, and accessible screening tools. This study investigated the diagnostic accuracy of C-reactive protein (CRP), serum amyloid A (SAA), and interferon gamma-induced protein 10 (IP-10) as potential screening tools. Methods. This cross-sectional diagnostic study investigated stored archived serum samples from three groups of subjects; bacteriology confirmed symptomatic TB group (n=57), probable TB (n=56) and healthy controls (n=60). CRP and SAA concentrations were measured using near point-of-care fluorescence immunoassay (NPOCT-FIA), while IP-10 was measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Diagnostic performance of individual and combined biomarkers was evaluated Results Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance of serum amyloid A (SAA) and C-reactive protein (CRP) for identifying confirmed tuberculosis (TB). Compared with probable TB and healthy controls, SAA achieved an AUC of 0.961 (cut-off >31.0 mg/L), with 96.5% sensitivity and 88.6% specificity, while CRP achieved an AUC of 0.953 (cut-off 21.3 mg/L), with 96.5% sensitivity and 86.0% specificity. Interferon gamma-induced protein 10 (IP-10) showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.545). Combined CRP and SAA achieved 100.0% sensitivity and 83.3% specificity. Conclusion: SAA and CRP met WHO target product profile criteria for TB triage screening.

after.authors: Zhou, Y.; Han, F.; Ma, Y.; Lu, Q.; Fang, Y.; Lou, K.; Wu, D.; Shen, Y.; Zhao, Z.
after.author_corresponding_institution: The First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University
after.abstract: Distinct tau-vulnerable and relatively spared subregions exist within the medial temporal lobe (MTL). However, it remains unclear that how functional connectivity (FC), anchored to tau-vulnerable MTL subregions, is related to tau pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and cognitive decline across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum. We here probe into this with resting-state fMRI data from a discovery cohort (ADNI; N = 386; cognitively normal [CN], mild cognitive impairment [MCI], and AD; 144 with 2-year follow-up) and an independent validation cohort at local hospital (N = 100; CN, subjective cognitive decline [SCD], and MCI; 25 receiving high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation [HF-rTMS]). We first separated the MTL into subregions with high and low neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) burden based on histological atlases, and calculated the seed-based whole-brain FC for each subregion. Second, group differences were assessed using ANCOVA, and associations with amyloid-{beta} (A{beta})/tau pathology, synaptic biomarkers, and cognitive performance were examined. Third, serial mediation, cross-lagged, and longitudinal regression analyses were performed to investigate the proposed pathological sequence, with additional evidence from HF-rTMS intervention and autopsy-confirmed Braak staging. Our results showed that, with the development of AD, FC reductions were focused on the high-NFT MTL network, particularly involving the inferior temporal gyrus and precuneus. Baseline tau burden in high-NFT MTL regions was able to predict subsequent FC alterations. Interestingly, FC between the high-NFT MTL and global brain showed region-specific associations with synaptic biomarkers, including negative associations in the cerebellum and positive associations in the precentral gyrus. We also observed a divergent association between the FC and cognition or pathology at different AD stages, shifting from positive in the early stages to negative in advanced AD. Serial mediation analyses supported a pathway linking tau burden to cognitive impairment through altered high-NFT MTL connectivity in the precuneus and occipital regions and subsequent synaptic dysfunction. Cross-lagged and longitudinal analyses further confirmed the proposed temporal sequence. Furthermore, HF-rTMS-related cognitive improvements were partially associated with enhanced synaptic plasticity through changes in precuneus-high-NFT MTL connectivity. Collectively, these findings support a spatiotemporal framework linking the dysfunction of tau-vulnerable MTL network to synaptic impairment and cognitive decline, highlighting high-NFT MTL-based FC as a potential imaging marker tracking AD progression.

after.title: Preprint: Decision for hysterectomy as a modifiable cardiovascular risk factor: A systematic review and meta-analysis
after.authors: Jayasundara, D.; Jayasingha, T.; Jayawardane, I.; Weliange, S. D. S.; Ratnasekera, I.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Colombo Faculty of Medicine
after.abstract: Objective: To describe the role of hysterectomy in modifying the major atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factors. Data sources: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and ScienceDirect were searched from database inception to March 10, 2026. Study eligibility criteria: Full-text randomized controlled trials, case-control studies, cross-sectional studies, cohort studies, case series, and experimental studies reporting new-onset cardiovascular events, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, or other metabolic effects following hysterectomy were eligible. Reviews and book chapters were excluded. Study appraisal and synthesis methods: Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by multiple reviewers with conflicts resolved by consensus. Cohort study quality was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; a modified version assessed cross-sectional studies. Meta-analyses were performed using a generic inverse-variance random-effects model for each outcome, stratified by study design (cross-sectional versus cohort) and effect measure (adjusted odds ratio, adjusted hazard ratio, or relative risk). Narrative synthesis was performed for outcomes not meeting criteria for meta-analysis. Results: Twenty studies (11 cohort, 8 cross-sectional, 1 mixed design) were included after screening 18,337 records from four databases. Hysterectomy was associated with significantly increased risk of hypertension (cross-sectional odds ratio 1.32, 95% confidence interval 1.18-1.48; cohort hazard ratio 1.19, 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.30), diabetes (cross-sectional odds ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval 1.11-1.32; cohort hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.29), hyperlipidemia (hazard ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.29), obesity (odds ratio 1.24, 95% confidence interval 1.03-1.50), and metabolic syndrome (odds ratio 1.24, 95% confidence interval 1.08-1.44). Conclusions: Hysterectomy is associated with increased risk of hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and metabolic syndrome, key modifiable atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factors. Active cardiovascular risk assessment and follow-up may be warranted for women who undergo hysterectomy, particularly at a young age.

after.authors: Baird, T.; Davey, T. R.; Chan, B. A.; Pattison, A.; Olagoke, O. S.; Littlejohn, M. L.; Greathouse, K. L.; Stone, J. K.; Fraser, T. A.; Webb, K. A.; Dunn, E. M.; Bell, P. T.; Dettrick, A.; Bint, M.; Sarovich, D. S.; Price, E. P.
after.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, yet the role of lower airway microbiota in disease development and progression is incompletely defined. Here, we characterised the lung microbiome in an Australian cohort (lung cancer n=106, healthy n=10) using shotgun metagenomics and semi-quantitative culture to evaluate site-specific microbial ecology across the tumour microenvironment (TME), contralateral airways, and oral cavity, to evaluate microbiome differences across early- and late-stage disease, and to quantify clinical covariate impacts on airway microbiota. Diversity analyses, multivariable linear modelling, and culture-based comparisons were performed, with adjustment for smoking pack-years, sex, and tumour characteristics. Cumulative smoking exposure caused significant, progressive core commensal depletion (Neisseria subflava, Gemella sanguinis, Rothia mucilaginosa), alongside Streptococcus mitis enrichment, with Mogibacterium diversum uniquely depleted within the TME of smokers. {beta} diversity in both early- and late-stage bronchial washes (BWs) significantly diverged from healthy controls, whilst Shannon diversity ( diversity) was significantly reduced in early-stage compared with late-stage BWs. The early-stage TME also demonstrated significantly reduced microbial cultivability compared with healthy and other lung cancer BWs. A small number of taxa were uniquely enriched (Sporothrix and Pseudomonas species) or depleted (Streptococcus parasanguinis, Streptococcus cristatus, R. mucilaginosa) within the TME, and 13 taxa were significantly enriched or depleted in both TME and contralateral airways compared with healthy airways. Only lung adenocarcinoma showed distinct oral {beta}-diversity restructuring. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that the lung cancer microbiome is characterised by early and progressive lower airway dysbiosis that is strongly shaped by tumour presence. Our findings point to potential new avenues for microbiome-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

MS genetic susceptibility and severity long after disease onset is well characterized, but the genetic architecture of disability severity near disease onset is unclear. We performed the first genome-wide association study of early MS severity to identify causal loci, prioritize effector genes and associated pathways, and understand the relationships of early MS severity and various traits. Methods: The primary outcome was the first age-related MS severity score (ARMSS), an age-adjusted severity measure, in 7,209 individuals of Swedish discovery cohorts and independent Italian and multi-national European replication cohorts. Replicated loci underwent conditional analysis, fine-mapping, time-to-event MS phenotype association analyses, and multi-omics-based gene prioritization. Using the genome-wide summary statistics, we also conducted heritability analyses, polygenic risk score association with other MS phenotypes, gene-level and pathway analyses, cross-trait analyses with disease-related traits, Mendelian randomization, and drug-repurposing screening. Results: Two suggestive loci were replicated: rs1234317 at chromosome 1 (effect allele T: beta = 0.100, SE = 0.0189, P = 1.08E-07) and rs929769 at chromosome 5 (effect allele T: beta = -0.0956, SE = 0.0184, P = 1.95E-07). Fine-mapping supported rs929769 as a single-variant 95% credible set, and rs1234317 and rs6657136 as a two-variant 95% credible set with two-causal-SNP model having the highest posterior probability. The SNPs did not show a significant change in effect sizes when adjusted for heritable traits and exhibited attenuated associations with long-term MS disability progression. TNFSF4 was the top prioritized effector for rs1234317, TNFSF18 for rs6657136, and ADAMTS2 for rs929769. Early MS severity showed partial genetic overlap with MS susceptibility or late MS severity, but no significant correlation with a range of neurological, psychiatric, autoimmune, cognitive, and aging traits. Pathway analyses identified ion-channel regulation and folic acid metabolism, and Mendelian randomization suggested nominal bidirectional associations with educational attainment. Drug screening nominated several drugs that can be repurposed. Discussion: This study identifies candidate causal variants of early MS severity and their effector genes: TNFSF4, TNFSF18, and ADAMTS2. It provides insights into the genetic architecture and therapeutic measures for the early phase of MS severity.

after.abstract: Background: attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic susceptibility and directional associations remain unclear. Methods: we analyzed European-ancestry genome-wide association study (GWAS) data for ADHD (38,691 cases; 186,843 controls) and BPD (12,339 cases; 1,041,717 controls). Linkage disequilibrium score regression, conjunctional false discovery rate (conjFDR), bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR), MR accounting for linkage disequilibrium and sample overlap (MR-LAP), Causal Analysis Using Summary Effect estimates (CAUSE), colocalization, and Sum of Single Effects (SuSiE) fine-mapping assessed genetic sharing and directionality. Results: genetic correlation was substantial (r_g = 0.733). ConjFDR identified 48 shared loci; 36 (75%) showed concordant directions in both phenotype-specific comparisons. Functional annotation implicated axon guidance, oxidative phosphorylation, and developing midbrain cells. ADHD-to-BPD MR was positive (22 instruments; inverse-variance weighted beta = 0.487, SE = 0.082, p = 3.27 x 10^-9), persisting after outlier removal, MR-LAP correction, and exclusion of two instruments at colocalized loci. Reverse MR was positive (five instruments; beta = 0.303, SE = 0.112, p = 6.83 x 10^-3) but heterogeneous and variant-sensitive. CAUSE favored directional over sharing-only models in both directions (delta ELPD = 6.98 and 5.92, respectively). SuSiE colocalization supported shared signals at rs17576773, rs9969232, and rs4727799. Conclusions: ADHD and BPD exhibit extensive genetic overlap involving 48 shared loci and convergent evidence of directional associations. Findings across complementary methods more consistently support an ADHD-to-BPD relationship, suggesting that shared genetic susceptibility alone may not fully explain their co-occurrence.

after.title: Preprint: Excluded causal variants produce false discoveries in genetic fine-mapping
after.authors: Weinstock, J. S.
after.abstract: Statistical fine-mapping seeks to distinguish causal genetic variants from correlated variants in linkage disequilibrium (LD). Although fine-mapping algorithms perform well in simulations, they are often applied in settings that violate their assumptions. In particular, genome-wide association study (GWAS) and quantitative trait locus (QTL) workflows routinely omit variants with minor allele frequency (MAF) below 1% and most insertions and deletions (indels), excluding many causal variants before fine-mapping begins. To assess this empirically, we compared filtered and unfiltered fine-mapping at 499 All of Us loci. Twenty percent of high-confidence calls after a 1% MAF filter, and 32% when indels were also omitted, lacked support in the unfiltered analysis. Errors were particularly enriched when tested variants tagged an omitted variant, so fine-mapping misassigned its signal to a proxy variant. At ABO, omitting the frameshift that defines blood group O gave near-certain posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs) to linked single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). To address this disconnect, we developed SuSiE-OUT, which enables fine-mapping in scenarios with possibly omitted causal variants. Modeling infinitesimal effects did not reliably prevent these errors, whereas imputing omitted variants or modeling them with our SuSiE-OUT method prevented most errors. Overall, we find that common analysis workflows substantially increase false discoveries in fine-mapping analyses, and we demonstrate two approaches to mitigate this challenge.

after.abstract: Objectives: Bilateral and trilateral selective antegrade cerebral perfusion (SACP) aim to ensure symmetric hemispheric perfusion during aortic arch surgery, which current monitoring cannot directly assess. As a step towards real-time monitoring, we assessed the feasibility of multichannel contrast-enhanced near-infrared spectroscopy (CE-NIRS) using indocyanine green and whether hemispheric bolus timing matched expectations for each perfusion configuration. Methods: In this prospective, offline-analysed pilot study, 10 patients undergoing aortic arch surgery (9 frozen elephant trunk) received 94 boluses across 10 perfusion configurations. The interhemispheric difference in time to peak ({Delta}TTP) was compared with the pre-bypass baseline using a linear mixed model with Holm correction, alongside cerebral oximetry; the relationship to postoperative cerebral injury was explored post hoc. Results: 92 of 94 boluses yielded a bilateral TTP. Contrary to expectation, the left hemisphere peaked later under bilateral (+7.2 s, 95% CI 3.4-11.0; p = 0.003) and trilateral SACP (+8.7 s, 2.5-14.8; p = 0.031). With both left-sided arch vessels on body perfusion, the asymmetry reversed (-7.0 s, -11.7 to -2.3; p = 0.025). {Delta}TTP detected 6 of 9 configuration effects, whereas oximetry detected none after correction. The three patients with cerebral injury showed the three most pronounced reversals (exact p = 0.100) but were also those managed trilaterally. Conclusions: Multichannel CE-NIRS is feasible during aortic arch surgery, without indicator-related adverse events. Bilateral and trilateral SACP did not secure symmetric indicator delivery; the configuration-dependent asymmetry and its reversal point to two steals within the perfusion circuit that oximetry missed. Their clinical relevance requires prospective confirmation.

after.abstract: Introduction: Dengue is under-recognized in Ghana, where laboratory testing is limited. We estimated dengue NS1 and/or IgM positivity among febrile patients and described geographical, temporal, and demographic variation. Methodology: We conducted cross-sectional surveillance among consenting febrile patients aged [≥]1 year at six public facilities in Greater Accra, Bono East, and Upper West between August 2023 and July 2025. We randomly selected one region within each of three ecological strata and selected facilities with high febrile-case volumes. We approached and recruited consecutive eligible patients. We tested serum for dengue NS1 antigen and IgM antibody by ELISA; positive NS1 samples underwent RT-PCR and serotyping. We estimated proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI) and used logistic regression to examine adjusted associations. Results: Among 2,936 participants, 204 were NS1- and/or IgM-positive (6.95%; 95% CI, 6.05-7.93%): 31 were NS1-only, 161 IgM-only, and 12 dual-positive. Prevalence ranged from 3.88% (95% CI, 2.19-6.31%) at Kintampo to 12.32% (9.56-15.55%) at Atebubu, both in Bono East. Adjusted odds increased with age (aOR per five years, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.05-1.14). Eight of 43 NS1-positive samples contained dengue RNA: five DENV-1 from Bono East and three DENV-3 from Upper West. There was no clear rainy-dry season difference. Conclusions: Dengue NS1 and/or IgM were detected among febrile patients at all six facilities, and RT-PCR confirmed circulation of DENV-1 and DENV-3. These findings support including dengue in febrile illness evaluation and strengthening laboratory-supported surveillance in Ghana. Keywords: dengue, febrile illness, NS1 antigen, IgM, DENV-1, DENV-3, Ghana

after.authors: Chatzilena, A.; Brooks-Pollock, E.; Colman, E.; Hansson, D.; Demiris, N.; Franklin, B.; Danon, L.
after.abstract: In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, most EU/EEA countries sequentially introduced non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) to reduce social contacts and mitigate transmission. The CoMix study captured real-time changes in social mixing, but substantial spatiotemporal gaps remain, with some countries lacking pandemic contact data. We developed a model-based framework to estimate time-varying changes in age-specific contact patterns and relate these changes to NPIs recorded in the ECDC-JRC Response Measures Database. This relationship was used to predict contacts during periods without CoMix observations. For countries without CoMix data, we reconstructed temporal age-specific mixing patterns using estimates from countries with pandemic contact data selected through a country-matching process based on socio-demographic characteristics and similarity in NPI implementation. We generated age-specific contact matrices for 28 EU/EEA countries spanning 2020-2022. Reconstructed patterns captured substantial temporal and cross-country variation in social mixing and its evolving association with NPIs across diverse European contexts. Our framework provides estimates that extend incomplete pandemic contact data across both time and countries, yielding a consistent set of age-specific contact matrices for the EU/EEA. These estimates address important gaps in empirical social-contact data and provide valuable insights into the interplay of NPIs and social mixing patterns which is of critical importance to improving epidemic modelling and policy making.

after.title: Preprint: Effect of starting metformin on severe and long COVID-19 among people living with type 2 diabetes in England: a new user cohort study in OpenSAFELY-TPP
after.authors: Amstutz, A.; Walker, V.; Madley-Dowd, P.; Denholm, R.; Zou, M.; Palmer, T. M.; OpenSAFELY Collaborative,  ; Eastwood, S. V.; Hulme, W. J.; Sterne, J. A. C.
after.abstract: Introduction: Observational studies report lower COVID-19 mortality among metformin users, but most used prevalent-user designs comparing long-term survivors with heterogeneous controls. Randomised trials suggest little or no mortality effect. No large observational study has used a new-user design to estimate the effect of starting versus not starting metformin on severe and Long COVID outcomes in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). We aimed to estimate this effect on COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, COVID-19 diagnoses, and Long COVID among adults with T2D in England. Research design and methods: Using OpenSAFELY-TPP linked NHS electronic health records, we conducted a population-based cohort study with a landmark new-user design. Adults aged 18-85 years newly diagnosed with T2D (August 2018-August 2019) were classified as starting metformin monotherapy within 6 months or not starting any antidiabetic drug, based on prescription data. Follow-up began 6 months after diagnosis and before the UK pandemic (avoiding immortal time) for up to 2 years. We estimated intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects using weighted Cox and pooled logistic regression, with negative (bone fracture) and positive (diabetes-related death) control outcomes. Results: Of 52,341 eligible people, 19,599 (37.4%) started metformin. For COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death, the maximally adjusted hazard ratio (HR) of metformin versus no antidiabetic was 1.17 (95% CI 1.02-1.35; 2-year risk difference 0.36%, 95% CI 0.09-0.62; intention-to-treat). The per-protocol HR for COVID-19-related hospitalisation or death was 1.11 (95% CI 0.96-1.29). The Long COVID estimate was imprecise (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.83-2.33; intention-to-treat). For bone fracture (negative control) the estimate was null (HR 1.00), but for diabetes-related deaths (positive control) it was elevated (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.09-1.81), indicating unmeasured confounding. Conclusions: The risks of severe and long COVID were slightly higher among people who started metformin, compared with those who did not start. These results plausibly reflect unmeasured confounding. These findings align more closely with randomised evidence than earlier prevalent-user studies and argue against a clinically meaningful benefit of starting metformin for COVID-19 prevention in newly diagnosed T2D.

Conclusions: The risks of severe and long COVID were slightly higher among people who started metformin, compared with those who did not start. These results plausibly reflect unmeasured confounding. after.abstract: Background: Elevated blood pressure (BP) in childhood is associated with cardiovascular risk, but its molecular lipid correlates remain poorly characterized. We investigated the association of plasma lipid species and patterns with concurrent and longitudinal BP phenotypes in school-aged children. Methods: In the Belgian ENVIRONAGE prospective birth-cohort, 195 children aged 9 to 12 years were examined between July 2021 and September 2024. A total of 1,232 plasma lipid species were quantified using liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-tandem mass spectrometry. Associations with systolic and diastolic BP percentiles were examined using multivariable linear regression with permutation-based family-wise error rate (FWER) correction. Lipid-set enrichment analysis, with P values from sample permutation to account for correlation among lipid species, evaluated coordinated associations. Significant findings were examined across longitudinal BP patterns in 177 children with BP measured at ages 4-6 and 9-12. Findings: Each 1-SD increase in triglyceride (TG) 58:9 fatty acyl (FA) 22:4 was associated with 7.36 higher systolic BP percentile points (95% CI=3.91-10.80; P_FWER=0.03). TG 58:9 FA 22:4 was associated with incident (OR=2.78; 95% CI=1.33-5.79) and persistent (OR=2.14; 95% CI=1.22-3.77), but not resolved elevated BP vs stable-normal BP. Among lipid sets, species with a total carbon number of 38, mainly PC and PE, were inversely enriched with diastolic BP percentile. Interpretation: Childhood BP was associated with higher levels of a highly polyunsaturated long-chain TG, closely related to current BP elevation and not elevated among children whose BP had normalized.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Uniformed Services University, Bethesda, MD 20814
after.abstract: The translation initiation factor eIF2 is an essential regulator of cellular protein synthesis with direct links to human physiology and development. Composed of eIF2, {beta}, and {gamma} subunits, eIF2 heterotrimer assembly requires the activity of its dedicated chaperone and the essential protein, CDC123. Accordingly, CDC123 is a key determinant of protein synthesis and cell growth. Previous research has demonstrated that variants in eIF2{gamma} impair neurodevelopment, and CDC123 variants of uncertain significance have recently been reported for pediatric patients with neurologic findings. However, the potential pathogenicity, and cell and molecular impacts of these clinically relevant CDC123 variants remains entirely unexplored. In this work, we describe four unrelated families with pediatric patients that present with neurodevelopmental delays, hypotonia, and motor dysfunction. The probands are heterozygous for three novel CDC123 missense variants. The potential pathogenicity of the variants is comprehensively assessed through appraisal of CDC123 variant allele frequencies, protein conservational analyses, structural modeling, and functional assays in both humanized yeast and human cell-based model systems. Cellular and biochemical studies indicated that the variants are damaging to CDC123 activity, altering CDC123-eIF2 subunit interactions and leading to reduced cell growth. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the CDC123 variants display dominant-negative effects on yeast cell growth and protein synthesis, rather than causing haploinsufficiency. Together, our findings provide the first link between CDC123 missense variants and human disease and highlight that CDC123-mediated eIF2 heterotrimer formation is essential for human development.

after.authors: WANG, D.; Hammond, C. J.; Salmeron, B. J.; Xiao, X.; Murray, L.; Gu, H.; Zhai, T.; Kuang, N.; Zheng, H.; Hill, J.; Lu, H.; Janes, A.; Ross, T. J.; Yang, Y.
after.abstract: Environmental exposures during childhood strongly impact individuals' cognitive and socioemotional development, and psychiatric vulnerability. However, childhood exposures rarely occur in isolation. Instead, they form a highly correlated 'exposome' whose multidimensional relationships with brain development and behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Elucidating the complex interplay between brain, behavior, and environment requires a multivariate approach. This study used regularized multiset canonical correlation analysis on longitudinal data from 8,113 preadolescents in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study to characterize latent multivariate dimensions linking diverse environmental exposures, tract-wisely resolved measures of white matter (WM) development and integrity, and multi-domain behavioral phenotypes and relate them to concurrent and future psychopathology. Two distinct multivariate dimensions were identified exhibiting different exposure, WM development, and behavior patterns. The first linked greater socioeconomic resources to more advanced WM development, particularly in dorsal-association tracts, and superior cognitive performance. The second dimension linked stronger psychosocial support with higher WM integrity, more advanced development of limbic tracts, and lower levels of psychopathology. Longitudinal analyses revealed differential contributions of these dimensions to follow-up cognitive, socioemotional and psychiatric outcomes. Moreover, WM and exposomic variates in these dimensions moderated the effects of childhood adversity on transdiagnostic psychiatric disorder risk, in sex- and context-specific fashions. Together, these findings clarify how childhood environmental exposures and the linked WM developmental differences relate to cognition and psychopathology risk, potentially informing the identification of candidate neural targets for future interventions.

after.authors: Riepenhausen, A.; Jacob, G. A.; Probst, T.; Klein, J. P.
after.abstract: The digital therapeutic priovi has small average effects for borderline personality disorder (BPD). In this preregistered secondary analysis, we aimed to explore the heterogeneity and potential moderators of these effects. Adults received priovi plus treatment as usual or treatment as usual alone. At the 3-month primary endpoint (N = 528), model-based recursive partitioning showed heterogeneous effects on Borderline Symptom List-23 (BSL-23) change (p = 0.022) and on clinically relevant response (p = 0.007). Benefit was larger at higher baseline symptom load: a representative tree split on Patient Health Questionnaire-9 at a score of 23, and the higher-score subgroup had roughly twice the BSL-23 reduction (conditional average treatment effects -0.40 versus -0.19). Baseline BSL-23, depressive symptoms, and recent life-threatening events ranked as the leading moderators. Quartile calibration of predicted CATEs was weak and non-monotonic. The moderators are hypothesis-generating and should not guide patient selection without external validation.

after.authors: Souza, B. R.; Guimaraes, J. S. d. F.; de Assis, M. M. R.; de Souza, E. M. S.; Fonseca, L. R. A.; Pires, A. C. V.; de Carvalho, I. R.; dos Anjos, K. C. C.; Nascimento, M. A. d. C.; Lima, M. C. S. B.; Castro, M. C. D.; Ferreira, M. E. M. d. A.; Mansur, V. F.; Oliveira, A. G.
after.abstract: The rapid expansion of online gambling and sports betting has raised concerns about gambling-related harm and its implications for public health. However, nationwide evidence regarding temporal trends and patterns of health care utilization associated with gambling remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. We conducted a nationwide retrospective study using administrative data from Brazil's Unified Health System from 2014 through 2025. We examined primary health care records associated with pathological gambling (ICD-10, code F63.0) and gambling and betting (code Z72.6). We analyzed temporal trends, seasonal patterns, and geographic and demographic distributions, calculating annual encounter rates per 100,000 inhabitants. Gambling-related primary health care encounters increased substantially during the study period, with a marked acceleration beginning in 2022. By 2025, nationwide rates reached 1.46 encounters per 100,000 inhabitants for pathological gambling and 0.60 per 100,000 for gambling and betting. Increases were observed across all five Brazilian regions, with the highest rates in the South and Southeast. Recorded encounters increased across age groups and both sexes, particularly among adults aged 20 to 39 years. Rates were also elevated among adolescent males and older women. Time-series analyses suggested seasonal variation, with higher indices generally between April and October. Gambling-related encounters in Brazilian primary health care increased markedly from 2014 through 2025, particularly after 2022, with substantial demographic and geographic variation. These findings indicate increasing documentation of gambling-related conditions within a nationwide public health system and underscore the need for improved surveillance, early identification, and access to appropriate mental health care.

after.abstract: Abstract Background and Objective: Pediatric emergency department (ED) visits for suicidal ideation and behavior have increased substantially, highlighting the need for scalable outpatient interventions that reduce recurrent ED use. We tested whether referral to outpatient crisis services was associated with fewer mental health-related ED revisits, hypothesizing that referred youth would have lower revisit rates than those receiving usual community care. Methods: We conducted a quasi-experimental study of 3,125 youth presenting with suicidal ideation or behavior to a large academic childrens health system between October 1, 2023, and August 31, 2025. Youth were referred to outpatient crisis services or community treatment (usual care) based on slot availability and clinician discretion. Propensity score modeling balanced demographic, clinical, and prior treatment characteristics between groups. Results: Among 3,125 qualifying index ED visits, 763 (24.4%) youth were referred to crisis services and 461 (14.8%) received [≥]1 crisis visit within 30 days. In intent-to-treat analyses, referral was associated with fewer mental health-related ED revisits at 90 days (adjusted incidence rate ratio [aIRR], 0.67; 95% CI, 0.56-0.81) and 180 days (aIRR, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.59-0.80). Associations were strongest among youth requiring short-term hospitalization (aIRR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.36-0.58) and those with moderate-to-high suicide risk (aIRR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.39-0.61). Findings were consistent in as-treated analyses. Conclusion: Outpatient crisis services were associated with substantially fewer mental health-related ED revisits among suicidal youth, with the largest reductions among youth with greater clinical acuity.

after.abstract: Objective: Schizophrenia (SZ) and bipolar disorder (BP) emerge in late adolescence or adulthood. Offspring at familial high risk for SZ (FHR-SZ) or BP (FHR-BP) are more likely to develop psychiatric disorders. Prior work from the Danish High Risk and Resilience (VIA) Study found sex-specific volumetric brain differences in offspring at FHR-SZ and FHR-BP aged 11-12 years. This study builds upon these findings by testing whether they reflect group differences in rate of change or stable group differences from early to mid-adolescence. Methods: This study investigated MRI data from offspring at FHR-SZ, FHR-BP, and population- based controls (PBC) at baseline (11-12 years; n=288) and follow-up (15-16 years; n=249). FreeSurfer longitudinal processing derived total brain volume, cortical measures, and intracranial volume (ICV). Linear mixed-effects models tested group-by-age interactions and sex-specific group effects, as well as associations with psychotic experiences (PE) and lifetime Axis-I mental disorders. Results: The analysis did not detect group-by-age interactions, indicating similar developmental slopes across groups. However, at both time points, males at FHR-SZ demonstrated reduced brain and cortical volumes compared to PBC and FHR-BP males. These effects were attenuated after adjusting for ICV, which was reduced in males at FHR-SZ. The analysis additionally detected volumetric reductions in males with PE, after controlling for risk status. Conclusions: These results extend the previous findings to ages 15-16 years, indicating group differences are stable and persist into mid-adolescence. Associations with ICV suggest early neurodevelopmental effects, and volumetric reductions in males with PE suggest convergent effects with FHR-SZ.

after.abstract: Reduced-dose pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) schedules (1+1; one primary and one booster) are now endorsed by the World Health Organisation under specific circumstances. Serotype-specific memory B cells (BMEM) are a marker of long-term protection but data from infant reduced-dose trials remain limited. As part of a randomised controlled trial in Vietnamese infants, we characterised serotype-specific BMEM responses in randomised subsets (N=50 per vaccine group per timepoint) following 0+1 (at 12 months of age) or 1+1 (2 and 12 months of age) schedules of PCV10 or PCV13, using a multimer spectral flow cytometry approach. after.authors: Reimer, D.; Repo, J.; Kilpi-Jakonen, E.; Palsdottir, K.
after.abstract: Aims: The November 2023 evacuation of Grindavik, Iceland, left families facing prolonged uncertainty about return. We examined adolescent well-being before and after evacuation and changes in gaps with national peers between 2025 and 2026. Methods: Repeated cross-sectional analyses used the 2023, 2025, and 2026 Icelandic Youth Study waves, adjusting for grade, gender, and non-Icelandic background. The town's single school in 2023 provided the pre-evacuation benchmark, with models accounting for national time trends. Adolescents who moved before evacuation provided a mobility benchmark. Results: In 2025, evacuees reported lower life satisfaction and school belonging, more psychosomatic symptoms, and higher odds of school absence and past-30-day substance use than the national reference group. The three well-being outcomes departed from the pre-evacuation pattern. Life-satisfaction and belonging gaps were larger among girls than boys in 2025, but these gender differences narrowed by 2026. Comparisons with prior movers suggested a distinct evacuation-related pattern in 2025 among evacuee girls, who reported lower life satisfaction and school belonging than prior-mover girls. In 2026, psychosomatic symptoms (B = 0.29, 95% CI [0.08, 0.49]), absenteeism (OR = 1.81, 95% CI [1.26, 2.60]), and substance use (OR = 2.59, 95% CI [1.75, 3.84]) remained higher relative to the national reference group. Life satisfaction and belonging were directionally lower, with intervals including zero. Change estimates did not establish narrowing of the gaps. Conclusions: The findings underscore the need for sustained educational and well-being support to address adolescents' social connections alongside their mental health during prolonged displacement, including in a Nordic welfare setting.

after.title: Preprint: Age-related Trust and its Association with Cost-related Medication Nonadherence
after.authors: Zhang, J. X.; Meltzer, D.
after.abstract: Trust operates foundationally at the personal and societal levels, a vital force that drives social connection, cooperation, and positive outcomes. In healthcare, trust is instrumental in improving patient outcomes as it forms the foundation for shared decision-making and patient-provider relationships. With growing evidence that generalized trust toward other people grows with age and behaviors such as cost-related medication non-adherence (CRN) decrease with age we study whether lack of trust is a force that drives up CRN and its variability in effects across age groups, controlling for other risk factors. The data consists of 680 Medicare diabetes patients at high risk of hospitalization enrolled in a randomized controlled trial of the effect of the Comprehensive Care Physician model (CCP) at an academic medical center between November 2012 and June 2016. This study provides first-of-its-kind evidence that lack of trust is an important force that drives up CRN and the effect of lack of trust decreased even though the lack of trust decreased by age increments. The effect of lack of trust is particularly pronounced among younger patients. For practice and policy, it shows the potential promising prospect that a more trusting attitude may be conducive to more productive health. More research is needed on how to build trust at the societal level and in healthcare specifically, and how generalized trust and target-specific trust of providers are correlated.

after.title: Preprint: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis
after.authors: van der Graaf, F.; Antonissen, N.; Scholten, E. T.; Schalkx, H.; Prokop, M.; Jacobs, C.
after.abstract: In this study, LLM and prompting strategies for labeling Specific Incidental Findings (SIFs) occurring during lung cancer screening, in radiology reports were compared. In this retrospective study, 300 CT reports from a Dutch academic hospital were included between 19th March 2003 and 28th December 2020. GPT-5, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3.1-8B-INST, MedGemma-4B-IT, a keyword-based search method, and a radiologist labelled the reports for the presence or absence of nine SIFs. The radiologist's scores were the reference standard. Each LLM was evaluated with four different prompting strategies: two without Chain-of-Thought (CoT), and two with CoT (one zero shot, one few shot). The automated labelling methods were evaluated against the radiologist primarily using Cohen's Kappa, and additionally sensitivity, specificity, and F1 scores. GPT-5 achieved substantial or almost perfect agreement for seven out of nine SIFs: aortic valve disease, bronchiectasis, consolidation, coronary artery calcification, emphysema, abnormality in mediastinal lymph nodes, and thyroid abnormalities, with Cohen $\kappa$ values of 0.81 (0.70, 0.93), 0.97 (0.93, 1.00), 0.71 (0.62, 0.82), 0.92 (0.87, 0.96), 0.91 (0.84, 0.97), 0.71 (0.62, 0.80), and 0.92 (0.86, 0.98) respectively. For the remaining two SIFs, moderate LLM agreement was obtained with MedGemma-4B-IT and with GPT-4-Turbo with Cohen $\kappa$ values of 0.48 (0.40, 0.60), 0.42 (0.31, 0.58) for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass respectively. The highest agreement was obtained with the non-CoT prompt strategies for most SIFs. This study demonstrated that LLMs can automatically label radiology reports with agreement ranging from almost perfect to moderate, but not one LLM -- prompt combination achieved the highest agreement across all SIFs.

after.title: Preprint: WALRUS: Robust and Transferable Deep Learning for Water and Lipid Removal in 1H-MRSI
after.authors: Fischer, H.; Motyka, S.; Weiser, P.; Strasser, B.; Hingerl, L.; Eckstein, K.; Chaknam, K.; Osburg, A. P.; Altmeyer, A.; Campilho, B.; Sazonova, E.; Li, Y.; Liu, J.; Dymerska, B.; Eftekhari, Z.; Shaw, T. B.; Barth, M.; Hangel, G.; Kaushik, S.; Haider, L.; Bogner, W.
after.abstract: Proton magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (1H-MRSI) enables non-invasive mapping of brain metabolism, but reliable quantification is challenged by residual water and extracranial lipid contamination. Recent work demonstrated that a deep learning model trained on simulated metabolite spectra combined with in vivo-derived water and lipid signals can outperform conventional nuisance-removal methods. However, this approach relied on heuristic simulation parameter distributions and a subject-specific L2-derived lipid estimate as an auxiliary network input, requiring subject-specific lipid masks and L2 processing during inference. Here, we introduce WALRUS (Water And Lipid Removal Using Spectral Learning), a fitting-consistent and empirically calibrated framework developed through a systematic evaluation of simulation realism, architectural priors, and network optimization. WALRUS uses the same metabolite basis as downstream spectral fitting and calibrates deliberately broadened simulation distributions from in vivo measurements. Controlled 7 T experiments demonstrate that empirical simulator calibration substantially improves nuisance removal and metabolite quantification compared with heuristic training distributions. With the optimized simulator, a capacity-matched comparison reveals no clear additional benefit from the L2-derived prior, allowing its removal and substantially simplifying inference. Further improvements are achieved with the final higher-capacity U-Net, while on-the-fly simulation improves generalization compared with training on a fixed synthetic dataset. The same framework was subsequently recalibrated and retrained at 3 T, where WALRUS outperformed conventional HLSVD+L2 processing on held-out data. Together, WALRUS combines these advances into an optimized framework that improves nuisance removal and downstream metabolite fitting, requires no subject-specific lipid segmentation or L2-derived auxiliary input during inference, and can be systematically adapted to different acquisition settings.

after.authors: Suri, H.; Keselman, Y.; Legel, L.; Govette, J.; Mullen, B.; Choradia, N.; Sartawi, T.; Abtin, F.; Moghanaki, D.; Thomson, C. C.; Yankelevitz, D. F.; Ahuja, Y.

after.abstract: Background: The Lung-RADS algorithm standardizes the management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules, but its risk assessment is driven chiefly by nodule size and attenuation. This misallocates a meaningful fraction of patients: a nontrivial share of small malignancies receive 12-month surveillance while large benign nodules proceed to invasive workup. Artificial intelligence (AI) may supply risk information independent of the imaging features Lung-RADS already uses. Methods: We validated LungAI, an investigational deep learning nodule malignancy classifier not yet cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), on the held-out NLST test partition of Ardila et al. (2,747 low-dose CT examinations from 1,244 patients with at least 1 solid or part-solid 4-30 mm nodule; 89 pathologically confirmed cancers, prevalence 3.2%). We compared discrimination against Sybil, mean nodule diameter, and estimated nodule volume. A board-certified radiologist assigned Lung-RADS v2022 categories to a positives-enriched random subset (226 eligible examinations; 78 cancers), projected to the full cohort by contingency weighting. A per-category reclassification algorithm shifted patients along the existing Lung-RADS management ladder using a-priori score cutpoints. We evaluated a separately locked follow-up configuration on examinations with a prior scan. Results: LungAI achieved AUROC 0.92 (95% CI 0.88-0.95) and AUPRC 0.47 (0.35-0.61), outperforming Sybil (delta AUROC 0.07; delta AUPRC 0.18), diameter (delta AUROC 0.14; delta AUPRC 0.34), and volume (delta AUROC 0.14; delta AUPRC 0.38; all P<0.001). Against Lung-RADS v2022 scored ordinally on the weighted annotated subset, LungAI improved AUPRC (delta AUPRC 0.31, P=0.003) but not AUROC (delta AUROC 0.03, P=0.20). LungAI added discriminative information independent of diameter (likelihood-ratio chi squared = 161, P < 10e-36; delta AUROC 0.10) and, on follow-up examinations, independent of delta diameter, volume doubling time, and new-nodule status (chi squared = 79, P < 10e-18). Integrated with Lung-RADS, LungAI reduced cancers on the slowest (12-month rescan) pathway by 46% (3.1 --> 1.6 per 1,000 examinations) and benign biopsy referrals by 20% (32.7 --> 26.2 per 1,000 examinations) at approximately unchanged total biopsy volume (51.0 --> 50.1 per 1,000). Assuming full adherence to recommended follow-up, the combined approach yielded 25 months of net diagnostic lead time, an estimated net cost saving of ~$2,200, and 6.5 fewer benign biopsies per 1,000 examinations; accounting for published adherence rates, it yielded 1.6 additional cancer diagnoses within 1 year per 1,000 examinations. Conclusions: LungAI contributes malignancy-risk information orthogonal to the size- and growth-based features underlying Lung-RADS and improves the allocation of screening patients across the existing management spectrum while potentially decreasing invasive procedures for benign lesions. Multi-site, multi-geography validation is required to demonstrate practical generalizability.

after.title: Preprint: Five Days of Acute Intermittent Hypoxia Is Safe and Improves Somatic Motor Function in Persons with Multiple Sclerosis
after.authors: Nehrujee, A.; Kalvakota, R.; Barry, A.; O'Shea, L.; Johnson, H. R.; Zou, C.; Northrop, J. N.; Mannella, K.; Dee, W.; Rymer, W. Z.; Nemeth, A. J.; Cohen, B. A.; Bright, M. G.; Sandhu, M. S.
after.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES Walking impairment affects up to 75% of persons with multiple sclerosis (MS), and the benefits of rehabilitation are constrained by limited capacity for training-induced neuroplasticity. Acute intermittent hypoxia (AIH), brief repeated exposures to low inspired oxygen, triggers serotonin-dependent spinal plasticity that enhances motor output. In spinal cord injury, daily AIH paired with walking training has produced larger walking gains than training alone, positioning AIH as a promising primer for rehabilitation. Before AIH can be combined with training in MS, its safety and stand-alone effects with repeated daily dosing must be established in a population with demyelinating disease. We therefore conducted the first multi-day AIH trial in persons with MS to characterize safety and tolerability and to evaluate preliminary effects on ankle strength and walking. METHODS Twenty-three ambulatory adults with MS (Expanded Disability Status Scale [EDSS] 3.0-6.5; 15 relapsing-remitting, 8 secondary-progressive) completed a randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Participants received AIH (15 x ~60 s episodes; FiO2 = 0.09; SpO2 target 84-88%) and Sham in a counterbalanced order, separated by a washout of at least 4 weeks. Assessments at pre-intervention, post-intervention, and follow-up included ankle plantarflexion and dorsiflexion torque, 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), Timed 25-Foot Walk (T25FW), and MS Walking Scale-12 (MSWS-12). Treatment effects were estimated using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with participant as a random effect. RESULTS No serious adverse events related to the intervention were reported, and follow-up MRI showed no new MS activity in either arm. Mean nadir SpO2 during AIH was 84.7 +/- 0.2%, and cardiovascular parameters returned to baseline within minutes of each session completion. Ankle plantarflexion torque was significantly greater following AIH than Sham (beta = 8.74 Nm, p < 0.001), with mean increases of 17.5% at post-intervention and 29.2% at follow-up. Six-minute walk distance was also significantly greater after AIH (beta = 10.14 m, p = 0.039). Dorsiflexion torque (p = 0.202), T25FW time (p = 0.239), and MSWS-12 score (p = 0.564) did not differ significantly between conditions. Greater elevation in heart rate during hypoxic episodes was associated with larger strength gains at follow-up (r = 0.58, p = 0.009). CONCLUSIONS: Daily AIH sessions are safe and well tolerated in persons with MS across a clinically heterogeneous disability range and produce significant improvements in ankle plantarflexion strength and walking endurance. These findings support combining AIH with task-specific gait training in future trials.

METHODS Twenty-three ambulatory adults with MS (Expanded Disability Status Scale [EDSS] 3.0-6.5; 15 relapsing-remitting, 8 secondary-progressive) completed a randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled crossover trial. Participants received AIH (15 x ~60 s episodes; FiO2 = 0.09; SpO2 target 84-88%) and Sham in a counterbalanced order, separated by a washout of at least 4 weeks. Assessments at pre-intervention, post-intervention, and follow-up included ankle plantarflexion and dorsiflexion torque, 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), Timed 25-Foot Walk (T25FW), and MS Walking Scale-12 (MSWS-12). Treatment effects were estimated using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with participant as a random effect. RESULTS No serious adverse events related to the intervention were reported, and follow-up MRI showed no new MS activity in either arm. Mean nadir SpO2 during AIH was 84.7 +/- 0.2%, and cardiovascular parameters returned to baseline within minutes of each session completion. Ankle plantarflexion torque was significantly greater following AIH than Sham (beta = 8.74 Nm, p < 0.001), with mean increases of 17.5% at post-intervention and 29.2% at follow-up. Six-minute walk distance was also significantly greater after AIH (beta = 10.14 m, p = 0.039). Dorsiflexion torque (p = 0.202), T25FW time (p = 0.239), and MSWS-12 score (p = 0.564) did not differ significantly between conditions. Greater elevation in heart rate during hypoxic episodes was associated with larger strength gains at follow-up (r = 0.58, p = 0.009). CONCLUSIONS: Daily AIH sessions are safe and well tolerated in persons with MS across a clinically heterogeneous disability range and produce significant improvements in ankle plantarflexion strength and walking endurance. These findings support combining AIH with task-specific gait training in future trials.
